english: Even monkeys fall from trees.
Fall down seven times, get up eight.
Three years on a cold stone still warms it. — Patience pays off.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

japanese: 案ずるより産むが易し
english: Giving birth is easier than worrying about it. — Fear is often worse than reality.
Time flies like an arrow.

japanese: 塵も積もれば山となる
english: Even dust, piled up, becomes a mountain.
To continue is strength.

japanese: 明日は明日の風が吹く
english: Tomorrow, tomorrow's wind will blow.
Dumplings over flowers. — Substance over style.

japanese: 井の中の蛙大海を知らず
english: A frog in a well knows nothing of the great sea.
After the rain, the ground hardens. — Hardship builds strength.

japanese: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず
english: Chase two rabbits and you'll catch neither.
Gold coins to a cat. — Pearls before swine.

japanese: 好きこそ物の上手なれ
english: What one loves, one grows skilled at.
The nail that sticks out gets hammered down.
Evidence over argument.
A cane before you stumble. — Better safe than sorry.
If you do it, it will be done.
If you are in a hurry, take the long way round.
One time, one meeting. — Treasure every encounter; it will not come again.
Learn the old to know the new.
Never forget the spirit of the beginner.
Flower, bird, wind, moon. — The beauties of nature.
One good deed a day.
Say it, then do it.
You reap what you sow.
Great talents mature late.
Single-minded, undistracted.
Progress by the day, advance by the month.
Unbending, unyielding.
Fair wind, full sails. — Smooth sailing.

japanese: 吾輩は猫である。名前はまだ無い。
english: I am a cat. I have no name yet.
attribution: Natsume Sōseki, I Am a Cat

japanese: 智に働けば角が立つ。情に棹させば流される。
english: Approach everything with reason, and you turn harsh. Row along on feeling, and you're swept away.

japanese: 雨ニモマケズ風ニモマケズ
english: Not losing to the rain, not losing to the wind.
attribution: Miyazawa Kenji, Ame ni mo Makezu

japanese: 世界がぜんたい幸福にならないうちは個人の幸福はあり得ない。
english: Until the whole world is happy, there can be no individual happiness.
attribution: Miyazawa Kenji, Night on the Galactic Railroad

japanese: 恥の多い生涯を送って来ました。
english: I have lived a life marked by much shame.

japanese: 人生は一行のボオドレエルにも若かない。
english: A single line of Baudelaire outweighs a whole life.
attribution: Akutagawa Ryūnosuke, Words of a Dwarf

japanese: はたらけどはたらけど猶わが生活楽にならざりぢっと手を見る
english: I work and I work, yet my life never grows easier. I stare at my hands.
attribution: Ishikawa Takuboku, A Handful of Sand

japanese: 山路を登りながら、こう考えた。智に働けば角が立つ。
english: Climbing the mountain path, I thought this: act by reason, and you become sharp-edged.

japanese: 願わくは花の下にて春死なんそのきさらぎの望月のころ
english: I wish to die beneath the blossoms in spring, near that full moon of the second month.

japanese: 行く河の流れは絶えずして、しかももとの水にあらず。
english: The river flows on without ceasing, yet the water is never the same water.

japanese: 祇園精舎の鐘の声、諸行無常の響きあり。
english: The bells of Gion Shōja echo the impermanence of all things.

japanese: 月日は百代の過客にして、行きかふ年もまた旅人なり。
english: The months and days are travelers of a hundred generations, and the years that come and go are travelers too.

japanese: 古池や蛙飛びこむ水の音
english: An old pond — a frog jumps in, the sound of water.

japanese: 見わたせば花ももみぢもなかりけり浦の苫屋の秋の夕暮
english: Looking out, there is neither blossom nor autumn leaf — only a thatched hut by the bay in the evening dusk.

japanese: 秋来ぬと目にはさやかに見えねども風の音にぞおどろかれぬる
english: Though autumn's arrival is not yet clear to the eye, the sound of the wind startles me into knowing it.
